claim.pdf_says:
NOTE 2    The STANDARD-BINARY mode of arithmetic is an obsolete feature.

Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in this facility will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove it from the next revision.  [second paragraph printed at the NOTE indent, in the smaller NOTE type face - it is a continuation paragraph of NOTE 2]
claim.markdown_says:
NOTE 2 The STANDARD-BINARY mode of arithmetic is an obsolete feature.

Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in this facility will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove it from the next revision.  [emitted as an ordinary top-level body paragraph, with no NOTE indent, no continuation marker, and no association with NOTE 2]
claim.why_it_matters: In ISO documents NOTE text is explicitly non-normative. Detaching this paragraph from NOTE 2 promotes it to what reads as normative body text sitting between general rules 2) and 3) of 11.9.5.2, so a reader or citation-checker can take 'interest in this facility will be reevaluated' as a requirement of the ARITHMETIC clause rather than as editorial commentary in a note.

verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED. Rendered p303 at 300 dpi and measured the glyphs; no content discrepancy exists.

(1) NOTHING IS MISPLACED OR MISSING. The paragraph is transcribed verbatim (character-for-character against the print) and sits in exactly the right document position: after 'NOTE 2 The STANDARD-BINARY mode of arithmetic is an obsolete feature.' and before general rule '3) If the STANDARD-DECIMAL phrase is specified...'. PDF reading order is 2) / NOTE 1 / NOTE 2 / Unlike... / 3) / 4); markdown order (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 13206-13216, work-unit page-303.md lines 6-16) is identical. The kind label 'misplaced-content' is therefore factually wrong - no content was moved, dropped, or reordered.

(2) THE CLAIMED 'NOTE INDENT' DOES NOT EXIST. Ink-column measurement of the left edge of every text line on the page: rule marker '2)' x=336 and '3)' x=337; the hanging-indent body lines of rules 2) and 3) x=409; NOTE 1 x=409/407; NOTE 2 x=409; the 'Unlike...' paragraph's three lines x=408/408/408. Notes are set at exactly the same left margin as the numbered rules' continuation text. Indentation carries ZERO information distinguishing note text from rule body text on this page, so the markdown cannot have 'lost the NOTE indent'. The claim misdescribes the PDF here.

(3) THE ONLY REAL DIFFERENCE IS TYPE SIZE - i.e. pure formatting. x-height measurement: rules 2) and 3) are 21 px on every line; NOTE 1 and all three lines of the 'Unlike...' paragraph are 19 px. So the claim's core typographic reading is correct - the paragraph is in the ~10% smaller NOTE face and is genuinely NOTE 2's second paragraph. But the markdown does not reproduce that 19px-vs-21px distinction for NOTE 1 or NOTE 2 either, nor for any of the 149 column-0 'NOTE' paragraphs in the file. Notes are identified throughout this transcription by their literal 'NOTE'/'NOTE n' tag, never by indent or type size. The refutation criteria explicitly exclude differences that are only formatting.

(4) THE CLAIM'S INTERNAL LOGIC IS SELF-DEFEATING. If a flat, unindented paragraph on this page 'reads as normative body text', that applies equally to NOTE 1 and NOTE 2, which the claim accepts as correctly transcribed. What actually marks note scope in the markdown is the 'NOTE n' tag plus paragraph adjacency, and the continuation paragraph both directly follows NOTE 2 and textually continues it ('Unlike other obsolete features...' answers NOTE 2's 'is an obsolete feature').

(5) PAGE 303 IS NOT ANOMALOUS - IT IS THE HOUSE STYLE. This same continuation paragraph is transcribed as an identical flat top-level paragraph at five other sites (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 9001, 13210, 32791, 45369, 47210). A document-wide transcription convention is not a page-303 content defect.

(6) THE CLAIMED HARM IS NOT CREDIBLE. The sentence contains no 'shall', states no requirement, imposes nothing on an implementation, and describes ISO's own intent about a future revision. No conformance requirement of the ARITHMETIC clause can be extracted from 'interest in this facility will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL', and no compiler behavior derives from it. There is no citation risk and zero impact on COBOL.NET.

Residual (cosmetic, NOT this finding): because the transcription strips note typography globally, an unlabeled note continuation paragraph is typographically indistinguishable from body text everywhere in the file - and the convention is applied inconsistently (at line 9012 an equivalent continuation was merged INTO the 'NOTE 1' paragraph instead of split off). If note/body marking is ever wanted, that is one document-wide styling decision affecting all 149 notes, not a structural per-page correction.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The paragraph is present verbatim and in the correct document position (immediately after NOTE 2, before general rule 3). The claim's premise about a lost 'NOTE indent' is wrong: measured left edges show notes at x=408-409, identical to the hanging-indent body text of rules 2) and 3) at x=409, so no indent distinguishes note from body text in the print. The claim's typographic reading is correct only as to size - x-height 19 px for the note face vs 21 px for body - but the markdown drops that size distinction uniformly for all 149 notes in the file, including NOTE 1 and NOTE 2 on this same page, and transcribes this identical continuation paragraph the same flat way at five other sites (lines 9001, 13210, 32791, 45369, 47210). That is formatting, not content. The text carries no 'shall' and no requirement, so it cannot be mistaken for a rule of the ARITHMETIC clause. Any change here would be a document-wide note-styling convention, not a page-303 structural fix.
